steward_gate.rule: Structural CI proves only that the exact candidate satisfies the trusted repository-side Steward structure contract. It never authorizes merge by itself. The single Main Steward must independently refresh live main, exact candidate head, required platform evidence, substantive exact-head review completion, unresolved findings and incident state immediately before an expected-head guarded merge, then verify resulting main. Candidate-executing CI must hold no status/check write authority and must not persist repository credentials. The trusted Steward workflow is base-owned and may publish only structural evidence. It resets the structural status to pending before every evaluation so a prior green result cannot survive a new review/base/label event. Trusted base code is checked out to a runtime-unique path so candidate content cannot pre-seed the trusted checkout location. Trusted gate artifacts are immutable in ordinary PRs; changing them requires the repository-side steward-meta-governance-reopen label, which is converted by the base-owned workflow into the fixed MAIN_STEWARD_LABEL signal. Open incidents fail closed unless their durable current event is explicitly NON_BLOCKING or the exact candidate is an explicit repair named by the incident contract. Incident history is append-preserved. Receipt prefixes must be normalized directory boundaries. A terminal candidate cannot alter completion-graph dependencies or semantics; completion-graph mutation at terminal is limited to a state-only closure of exactly one previously ACTIVE bounded node. PR structural diffs use merge-base-to-head semantics; main push structural diffs compare the exact previous and current trees. The first Steward-gate bootstrap cannot trust a base checker or base-owned workflow that does not yet exist, publishes no trusted Steward status, and therefore requires explicit live Steward review plus the ordinary exact-head platform proof.

external_enforcement.desired: After Steward-gate bootstrap, GitHub branch protection or a repository ruleset should require the three exact-head platform check contexts plus the trusted n0te2-steward-structure context where administratively available.
external_enforcement.current_truth: Repository policy and trusted structural CI define evidence requirements, while the single active Main Steward remains the live merge-authorization owner unless external branch protection or ruleset evidence proves equivalent atomic enforcement. A structural status, including green, is not a merge receipt.
